findings.reason: citing the existing lift record and lease lets §3/§4 extend them rather than add two parallel mechanisms, and the §2 report's own repair direction already points at the per-project record.
findings.text: the design re-invented machinery it did not search for: §3's "append-only record of lifts beside the run" duplicates `recovery_log_path` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:329`), which the sweep already writes append-only on every lift, one line per sweep carrying each resumed run's id and hold signature (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:1374`; the §2 report reads two such lines, recovery/nova.jsonl 7668–7669, with the same hold `wait:65cbdbf2402325fa`); and §4's "claim on its worker session" duplicates `HostLease` (`reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26`), the existing single-owner claim with atomic create/renew/release and stale expiry already wrapped by `watch_host_lease` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:148`); §4 also parallels the existing live-writer guard `member_in_flight_verdict` (`reckon/crew/node.py:357`)

findings.reason: the section must either extend the lease or state the property the lease lacks, rather than add a parallel claim with no justification.
findings.text: §4 adds a session claim whose semantics (single owner for a lifetime, atomic take, release on exit, a stale claim must not block forever) are exactly `HostLease`'s (`reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26`, `LEASE_STALE_SECONDS`), and the lease centrally owns the renew/release/atomic-link logic a hand-rolled claim would have to restate

findings.reason: a forked claim drifts from the lease owner and a forked lift record from the recovery log; the owner files to extend are `reckon/crew/host_lease.py` and `reckon/crew/resumption.py`.
findings.text: §4 owns a second single-owner claim beside `reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26` (`HostLease`, used via `watch_host_lease` at `reckon/crew/runs.py:148`), and §3 owns a second append-only lift record beside `reckon/crew/resumption.py:329` (`recovery_log_path`, written at `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1374`)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; both sections edit the existing owner modules behind the `resume_plan`/`_launcher_refusal` pair the plan already names, so no shallow-wrapper sprawl is added.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — two shared mechanisms are forked: §3's per-run lift record (owner `reckon/crew/resumption.py:329`) and §4's session claim (owner `reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1593, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 adds a live-session refusal beside the two existing live-process refusals and a claim surface without naming what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the design cites the guards it edits but misses two mechanisms it re-invents: §3's append-only lift record duplicates `recovery_log_path` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:329`) and §4's session claim duplicates `HostLease` (`reckon/crew/host_lease.py:26`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's session claim is a thin layer over single-owner lease machinery that already exists, with no statement of why `host_lease.py` cannot carry the session.
